content.introduction: The tide is the only renewable source you can put in a diary. Wind drops and the sun sets, but the moon keeps an appointment, and a tidal lagoon can be scheduled against a grid four years ahead.
content.markRationale: A ring holding a tide line. The line is not flat, because water in a vessel is not flat. It is an arc struck at three times the radius of the ring, sitting a quarter of a radius below centre, which is what gives the mark its lift.
content.colourRationale: Deep grounds everything and Chalk carries the page. Tide is for surfaces and charts. Beacon marks the single most important thing on a page and never more than three percent of it.
content.typeRationale: Archivo sets headings, the wordmark and any number a reader has to compare, because its figures are why it was chosen. Literata sets anything read for more than a line, and it prints well on the uncoated stock the annual review uses.
misuse: Do not stretch. Scale both axes together, always.
Do not rotate. The tide line is level or it is nothing.
Do not recolour outside the approved colourways.
Do not add a shadow, a glow, a bevel or an outline.
Do not place it on low contrast. Use the reversed mark.
Do not retype the wordmark. It is artwork, not live text.
content.constructionNotes: The ring is five units in a twelve unit square, with a stroke of nine tenths of a unit. The tide line is an arc of three times the ring radius, crossing a quarter of a radius below centre. Everything is a whole fraction of r, so the mark rebuilds from one number.
